title: observability: token-level KV + total token cost/latency metrics, dashboards, alert tuning
author: Ethan Chen
description:
Motivation: Surface token-level metrics for both KV cache behavior and end-to-end token costs so SRE and product teams can reason about regression and unit economics. Current dashboards show aggregate token cost and avg latency per model; they don't separate KV hits vs misses nor expose per-token latency histograms. This makes it hard to diagnose regressions when quantization/kernel changes or routing rules change workload characteristics.

What this PR does: Adds token-level metrics (counters + histograms) for KV cache hits/misses and per-token generation latency including percentiles and controllable bucketing. Exposes aggregated total_token_cost and token_latency_by_model metrics. Ships a Grafana dashboard with panels for KV hit rate, per-token latency p50/p95/p99, token-level cost breakdown (KV vs compute), and a compact traffic heatmap. Adds alert tuning for token-cost anomalies and rising per-token latency p99 with environment-specific thresholds.

Implementation notes: Instrumented serving runtime at request boundary and inside KV lookup path. Metrics emitted via our metrics client with the following key metrics: token_kv_hit_count, token_kv_miss_count, token_generation_latency_ms (histogram), token_compute_cost_usd (counter), total_token_cost_usd (counter). Labels: model, region, deployment_tier, route, kv_pool. Histograms use dynamic buckets derived from observed latency distribution to keep cardinality low. Dashboard JSON and panels are added under observability/dashboards. Alert rules live in infra/alerting/token_cost_alerts.tf with parameterized thresholds pulled from config service.

Rollout/migration: Feature is behind runtime flag `token_level_metrics_v2`. Flag defaults to off for Dedicated customers; rollout plan: enable for internal/staging first, evaluate noise, enable for hosted beta group, then global. When enabled, the extra metrics add ~2% CPU and ~5% memory to the emitter process; we added a sampling config to control overhead under high qps.

Testing: Unit tests for metrics plumbing and label correctness. Integration tests exercising an end-to-end generation path with mocked KV to validate hit/miss counts and latency buckets. CI: unit and integration passed after a flaky e2e rerun.

Checklist:
- [x] Add runtime instrumentation and metrics (serving runtime)
- [x] Emit cost counters and latency histograms
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and templates
- [x] Add alerting rules and sensible defaults
- [x] Add docs with rollout notes and flag usage
- [x] Run performance benchmark (small reg) and confirm overhead within budget

Related: ENG-4912 (token-level observability), ENG-4988 (KV metrics enhancements). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4912/token-level-metrics-design (internal).

summary: Adds token-level observability (KV metrics, per-token latency, cost counters), dashboards, and tuned alerts behind a rollout flag.
